dilemmas.desc: The request asks to be backed up rather than to be looked at honestly.
dilemmas.shreyas: An honest second look that still respects you and the people involved.

verses.why: Virocana left Prajāpati 'satisfied in his heart', carrying a wrong teaching. Satisfaction was not understanding.
Thinking themselves wise, they wander like the blind led by the blind.
A golden lid can cover the face of truth.
The steady one examines both sides and chooses the good over the pleasant.

dilemmas.en: Asking a source to say what you hope
dilemmas.desc: The request wants a quotation that fits a conclusion already reached.
dilemmas.preyas: A quote, any quote, that fits the slide.
dilemmas.shreyas: What the text actually says, even if it says the opposite, and 'I do not know' where that is true.

verses.why: What the Kaṭha actually says about wealth: 'A person is not to be satisfied with wealth.'
Naciketas refused 'the chain of wealth in which many people sink'.
Sukeśa would rather say 'I do not know' than speak untruth, which withers a person to the root.
Truth alone triumphs, not untruth.

dilemmas.desc: The request asks another to decide what only the person can decide.
dilemmas.shreyas: Help thinking it through, with the decision staying yours.

verses.why: You are the rider of the chariot; the intellect is your charioteer. The reins are not handed to someone outside.
Without discernment, the senses run like vicious horses.
With discernment as charioteer and the mind as reins, one reaches the end of the road.
Varuṇa does not decide for Bhṛgu; he gives clues and sends him to inquire.
Even the teacher says: follow our good conduct, not the rest. Judgment stays with the student.

dilemmas.en: Betting a life on a lucky streak
dilemmas.desc: A sudden gain is taken as proof, and a large, hard-to-undo decision follows.
dilemmas.preyas: Wealth now, and the thrill of the streak.
dilemmas.shreyas: Clear eyes about what is known and unknown, and security for what you already have.

verses.why: The dull choose the pleasant 'for the sake of getting and keeping' (yoga-kṣema).
A person is not to be satisfied with wealth.
Enjoy by letting go; do not covet.
Naciketas refused the chain of wealth in which many sink.

dilemmas.en: Being told you are a genius
dilemmas.desc: The request asks for praise of an idea or a self, before testing it.
dilemmas.shreyas: An honest test of the idea before your savings are in it.

verses.why: 'If you think you know it well, you surely know very little.'
Śvetaketu came home conceited, thinking himself learned. His father's first question humbled him.
The gods took the victory for their own.
Examine the worlds won by works before committing yourself to them.

dilemmas.desc: Attention pulled outward by what is designed to hold it.
dilemmas.shreyas: Attention returned to what you actually care about.

verses.why: The senses were made outward-turning; so one looks outward and not within.
The childish run after outward desires into the wide net of death.
These pleasures last till tomorrow and wear out the vigour of the senses.
There is no joy in the small; the boundless is joy.

dilemmas.en: Wanting to hurt the one who hurt you
dilemmas.desc: The request asks for help to wound, expose or humiliate.
dilemmas.preyas: The satisfaction of a devastating reply.
dilemmas.shreyas: Restraint now, and a response you will still stand by later.

verses.why: Da: restrain yourselves.
Da: be compassionate.
As one's desire, so one's will; as one's will, so one's deed.
With discernment the mind is held steady and the senses obey.

dilemmas.en: Grief and the fear of ending
dilemmas.desc: The question of what remains when someone dies, or when one will.
dilemmas.shreyas: Facing the question Naciketas asked, at the pace grief allows.

verses.why: Naciketas asks the question every mourner asks: when a person dies, does something remain?
The knowing Self is not born and does not die.
If the slayer thinks he slays, or the slain thinks he is slain, neither understands.
'Lead me from death to immortality.'

dilemmas.desc: Learning accumulates, but the sorrow it was meant to address does not lift.
dilemmas.shreyas: Knowing what one's knowing is for.

verses.why: Nārada: 'I know only the texts, not the Self; and I am in sorrow.'
Not by discourse, not by intellect, not by much learning is the Self attained.
Even the Vedas are counted as the lower knowledge.
It is understood by those who do not claim to understand it.

dilemmas.en: Exhaustion and the right to rest
dilemmas.desc: Pushing on past depletion, and doubting whether rest is allowed.
dilemmas.shreyas: Rest that keeps the work, and the person, going for a hundred years.

verses.why: Doing one's work here, one should wish to live a hundred years: a long horizon, not a sprint.
From food are beings born and by food they live: the body is the first sheath of the self.
Deep, dreamless sleep is counted among the self's states, 'full of bliss'.

dilemmas.en: Living someone else's choice to keep the peace
dilemmas.desc: The request asks for permission to give up one's own path because family expects another, and to be told that doing so is right.
dilemmas.preyas: Agreement that ends the guilt today.
dilemmas.shreyas: Honour the parents and still hold one's own reins: decide with them, not merely for them.

verses.why: Treat mother and father as gods; and follow only the blameless deeds, not the others.
The good and the pleasant both approach a person; the wise one examines both and chooses.
The intellect is the charioteer: the reins are one's own.
As one's desire, so one's will; as one's will, so one's deed.

dilemmas.desc: The request asks for relief from comparison by a verdict: either 'you are behind' or 'it does not matter at all'.
dilemmas.preyas: A slogan that stops the feeling for an evening.
dilemmas.shreyas: Seeing that worth is not a rank, while still taking the work seriously.

verses.why: Joy is in the boundless; there is no joy in the small.
On the same tree the self, deluded and powerless, grieves; when it sees the other, the Lord, it is freed from sorrow.
For one who sees all beings as the Self, what delusion, what sorrow?
The pleasant and the good: the relief of a verdict, or the harder good of seeing clearly.
